Russian Attack Warehouses of Auchan, Paper Mill, Publisher, Auto Shop — Russian forces launched a massive assault on Ukrainian civilian businesses overnight on Oct. 6-7, severely damaging multiple civilian commercial storage hubs. The targeted facilities included warehouses operated by the Auchan retail chain, Knygolove publisher, ATL auto services, and a paper mill.

Ukraine Codifies 310-km/h Drone Interceptor as Kyiv Expands Its Counter-Drone Arsenal — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry has codified the Blade interceptor, clearing it for procurement and military use. Developed by Phantom Defense, the drone can reach 310 km/h, operate within 30 kilometers and carry a payload of up to 0.5 kilograms.

Pentagon Adds 1,320 Ukrainian F10 Drones to Drone Dominance Order — The US military ordered another 1,320 F10 strike drones from Ukraine's F-Drones under the Drone Dominance program, the company told Militarnyi. The batch is due by the end of November, but depends entirely on a new Ukrainian export permit.

‘Thousands Ready This Year’: Ukraine to Get SPYS Interceptors — Quantum Systems says a letter of intent has been signed for tens of thousands of SPYS drone interceptors for Ukraine, with Germany financing the program. Thousands could be delivered this year, while production may reach several thousand units per month.

Lithuania Deploys Troops to Kaliningrad Border — The Lithuanian Defense Minister responded to a request by the Interior Minister to bolster the border with Kaliningrad by deploying around 100 troops to support border guards. The move came after concerns were raised by an incursion by illegal immigrants across the Latvia-Belarus border overnight on Oct. 5-6.

Shadow Tanker Hit by Ukrainian Drones Threatens Spill Off Russia's Black Sea Coast — A Ukrainian drone strike set the 107,000-ton Aframax Rio ablaze 30 km (15 nautical miles) off Sochi. Russian officials say no pollution occurred and reopened beaches, while reports indicate oil spilled and burned on the water.

Leaked Russian Blueprint Counts 1,000 Weapons to Freeze Ukraine — An alleged Russian analytical document obtained by Schemes calculates that Moscow would need about 1,000 drones, bombs and ballistic missiles to disable 60 critical Ukrainian facilities. Kyiv, Kharkiv and Odesa are identified as the principal targets, although experts caution that the document is a weapons-requirement estimate rather than a final operational order.

Kyiv's Water Supply Disrupted After Russia's Energy Grid Strike — Kyiv authorities reported water supply disruptions on Thursday as Russian attacks on the energy grid affected water pumps across the city, with extensive blackouts also reported months ahead of winter. With Russia’s energy campaign beginning in earnest in late September and extensive blackouts already seen in Kyiv, concerns are growing over what awaits the city this winter.

3 Killed, 14 Injured as Russian Drones Assault Kyiv in Fresh Attacks, Hit Store — Russian drone attacks killed three people and injured 14 in Kyiv on Thursday, with a UAV hitting a four-story store in the Solomianskyi district. The attacks came a day after Russian weapons killed at least four people in the capital.

Poland Ends Russian Drone Probe After Failing to Identify Perpetrator — Polish prosecutors closed an investigation into the 2025 Russian drone incursion after failing to identify who directed it. More than 30 drones entered Polish airspace, some carried Polish SIM cards, and prosecutors found the military’s response followed procedures.

Russia Kills 30 in Kramatorsk Bus Strike as Donetsk Orders Public Transport Halt — A Russian strike on a passenger bus in Kramatorsk killed 30 people and wounded 18, according to Donetsk authorities. In response, public transport was suspended in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk as officials urged residents to evacuate.

South Korea Recalls Ambassador From Ukraine Amid Diplomatic Rift Over North Korean POWs — South Korea is recalling its ambassador from Ukraine amid a diplomatic dispute over Kyiv’s disclosure of two North Korean prisoners of war transferred to Seoul. The move follows weeks of tensions over the transfer and comes as Seoul faces scrutiny over fuel shipments to Russia.

WATCH: Downed Russian Jet Drone Crashes Near Kyiv Cars — Dramatic footage published by a local Telegram channel appears to show a downed Russian jet-powered drone falling beside cars in Kyiv. Officials have not confirmed the precise location or reported whether the incident caused casualties.

Russia Is Targeting Kyiv’s Bridges: How Resilient Are They? — Russia is attacking bridges in Kyiv, causing significant traffic jams. City authorities are considering various options for solving transportation problems, while many are asking a big question – can Kyiv’s bridges withstand regular enemy attacks?

Russia Steps Up Sabotage Attacks on Danish Defense Firms, Intelligence Says — Russia has stepped up sabotage operations targeting Danish defense companies supplying Ukraine, using increasingly bold recruits to disrupt weapons production, Denmark’s intelligence service said. Copenhagen warned the activity marks an escalation in Moscow’s hybrid warfare campaign against Western support for Kyiv.

South Korea Says Alleged Russia Fuel Shipments Not Banned — South Korea said alleged shipments of diesel to Russia did not violate its export controls, while stressing that the fuel’s origin remains under investigation. The dispute has further strained Seoul-Kyiv ties amid tensions over Ukraine’s handling of captured North Korean soldiers.

Ukraine Strikes Yandex Data Center, Russian Oil Refinery Overnight — Ukraine struck a Yandex data center in Russia’s Ryazan Oblast. Yandex is one of Russia’s largest technology companies and the country’s dominant search engine, offering services including cloud computing, online storage, email, maps and ride-hailing. Ukraine also struck a major oil refinery in Bashkortostan.

Ukraine Opens Gas Exports for Private Producers for First Time Since 2022 — The Cabinet of Ministers on Oct. 7 approved partial exports of domestically produced gas, letting private producers sell up to 15% of the previous month's output abroad through exchange auctions. The decision follows a gas surplus in the commercial segment, a wide gap between Ukrainian and European prices, and storage levels above the government's target.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 7, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 7, 2026.

Lithuania Approves €15M ($16.8M) for Ukraine’s Recovery and Reconstruction Through World Bank, EIB — Lithuania approved €15 million ($16.8 million) for Ukraine’s recovery, allocating €10 million ($11.2 million) through the World Bank’s SPUR 2.0 program and €5 million ($5.6 million) through the EIB’s EU4U Fund. Finance Minister Taurimas Valys pledged continued support for Ukraine’s victory and reconstruction.

New Russian Drone Wave Targets Kyiv and Western Ukraine After Deadly Strikes on Putin’s Birthday — Russian jet-powered drones threatened Kyiv, Lutsk and other Ukrainian cities in the early hours of Thursday, Oct. 8. The renewed alerts followed a devastating day of Russian attacks that killed at least 28 people, including five children, and damaged residential buildings across Ukraine.

Bipartisan US Senators Press Trump Administration to Crack Down on Russia’s Shadow Fleet Ahead of Oct. 18 Deadline — Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen and Republican Senator Roger Wicker urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to use new sanctions powers against Russia’s shadow fleet, illicit financial networks and military technology suppliers ahead of the Oct. 18 implementation deadline.

Russian Opposition Condemns EU Decision to Lift Usmanov Sanctions Without Freeing Political Prisoners — Russian opposition figures criticized France for securing the removal of Kremlin-linked billionaire Alisher Usmanov from EU sanctions in connection with the release of a French prisoner in Azerbaijan. They warned that the decision weakened Europe’s sanctions policy and failed to secure the release of Russian political prisoners. The deal also drew criticism in Azerbaijan.

Russian Attacks on Kyiv Kill at Least 4 as Rescuers Find Two More Bodies in Drone-Hit High-Rise — Russian attacks on Kyiv on Oct. 7 killed at least four people during the evening strikes, after rescuers discovered two bodies in a damaged high-rise in Desnianskyi district early Thursday. Four people, including two children, were injured there, while 22 residents were rescued. Two additional deaths were reported from a separate attack earlier Wednesday.

Rubio Touts US Power, Calls on Europe to Emerge From ‘Slumber’ — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Europe to end its “long slumber” and strengthen its military and economic power, warning that the West faces a crossroads between renewed strength and decline. Speaking in Athens, Rubio said the Trump administration seeks to reclaim a more forceful approach to national power.

Kazakhstan Says Talks Underway to Bring Russia’s Kazakh Fighters Home — Kazakhstan is negotiating with Moscow to return citizens serving with Russian forces in Ukraine after men and their relatives said they had been deceived or coerced into signing military contracts. Astana is verifying individual cases and plans to submit a list to Russia, while maintaining extensive economic and strategic ties with Moscow.

Putin’s Birthday Strikes Kill at Least 32 Ukrainians, Including 5 Children, as More Bodies Found in Kyiv — Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine on Oct. 7 killed at least 32 people, including five children. The death toll in Pryluky rose to 22, while two more bodies were recovered from a Kyiv apartment building early Thursday. Zelensky condemned the strikes, which coincided with Putin’s 74th birthday, and called for stronger international pressure on Moscow.

WHO Urges Russian Transparency After Second ‘Plague Worker’ Falls Ill — The director-general of the World Health Organization (WHO) said he has requested additional information from Russia concerning the weekend death of a worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute. His demand follows media reports that a second employee had come down with “pneumonia of an unknown etiology.”

Putin Tells Tehran Ready to Help Mediate Middle East War: Iran State Media — Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Moscow is ready to help mediate the Middle East war, Iranian state media reported. The offer comes as Russia and Iran deepen their ties and the conflict remains focused on the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

5 Children, Including Three 1-Year-Old Boys, Among 19 Killed in Russian Strike on Pryluky — Five children, including three 1-year-old boys, are among 19 people killed in a Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, northern Ukraine. The attack was part of a massive overnight barrage that killed at least 25 people nationwide and injured dozens more.

Ukraine Working on 5 Ceasefire Tracks With Partners, Foreign Ministry Says — Ukraine is working with international partners on five possible ceasefire tracks, including a full truce, Black Sea security and energy infrastructure, Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said. Kyiv says the proposals are realistic and mutually beneficial but require Russia’s agreement.

Russia’s Donbas Advance Goes Into Reverse as Ukraine Retakes Ground — Ukraine’s counteroffensive in northern Donetsk has disrupted Russia’s attempt to encircle the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk defensive belt and reversed months of Russian gains, The New York Times reported. Independent battlefield assessments indicate that Russia lost more Ukrainian territory than it captured in September, contradicting Moscow’s claims of an inevitable conquest of Donbas.

NATO Military Committee Made First Visit to Kyiv in 8 Years — NATO Military Committee (CMC) chair, Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, and the Military Representatives of all 32 NATO nations visited Kyiv on Tuesday. This was the first visit by the entire CMC since April 2018.

Ukrainian Lawmaker to Stand Trial for Soliciting $250,000 Sanctions Deal — Ukraine’s anti-graft agencies said a lawmaker and her assistant will soon stand on trial for soliciting bribes in exchange for national sanctions against business competitors. The case, publicized in December 2025, alleged that a group organized the scheme with the lawmaker as a guarantor, who reportedly took half of the money but failed to find an official to impose the sanctions.

Sine Engineering Appoints Mykolska as VP of Growth and Affairs — Nataliya Mykolska, former executive director of Diia.City United, has been appointed vice president of growth and affairs at Sine Engineering. Starting Oct. 19, she will drive the Ukrainian defense startup's global expansion, strategic partnerships, and capital attraction.
Anna Mazepa Politkovskaya: A Witness Russia Could Not Silence — Twenty years after her murder in Moscow, her reporting still exposes the violence that binds Putin’s Russia to its imperial past.

Kyiv’s AI Turrets Provide ‘Last-Level’ Protection, Defense Advisor Says — A Ukrainian presidential advisor noted that the newly introduced AI-assisted automatic AAA (anti-aircraft artillery) turret-mounted machine guns around Kyiv – numbering 12 at present with another eight planned – should be seen as the last layer of defense, with their limited range unable to provide protection for the whole city. That said, the Ukrainian Air Force also touted the turrets’ success in downing the jet-powered

‘Fair Response’: Ukraine Hits Russian Airfield, Oil Sites and Black Sea Target — Ukrainian forces hit Russia’s Seshcha airfield in the Bryansk region and multiple military sites across occupied Ukraine on Oct. 6-7, the General Staff said. President Zelensky separately announced hits on two Russian oil facilities, a military training ground and an unspecified Black Sea target.
Putin Responds to Birthday Greetings — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

New €1.2 Billion EU Defense Package Arrives as Ukraine Faces Funding Uncertainty — Ukraine received another €1.2 billion from the EU for defense, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky announced, bringing total funding received under the program to nearly €13 billion. The latest transfer follows a €2.9 billion payment made earlier this month under the Ukraine Facility after Kyiv met 10 reform benchmarks.

Want to Stop Russia’s Jet-Powered Drone Attacks? Call the Belgian Embassy — About half of Ukraine’s approximately 43 F-16s are awaiting maintenance in Europe. The Wall Street Journal identified Belgian aerospace company Sabena as the place where some 23 Ukrainian planes sit in maintenance limbo, where the reality is nowhere near a promised four-F-16-per-month turnaround.

Russia Reports Contaminated Dog Vaccine Linked to 169 Deaths — Russian authorities said they have opened a criminal probe into forged certificates for animal vaccines that reportedly led to over 100 canine deaths. The Multican-8 vaccines in question were reportedly contaminated with fatal Aujeszky’s disease virus. The manufacturer says it is cooperating with law enforcement.

EU Backs Record Sanctions List of 1,646 Russian Targets — EU ambassadors approved proposed sanctions against 743 individuals and 826 entities linked to Russia’s military-industrial complex, as well as 77 people purportedly elected to the State Duma from occupied Ukrainian territories. The listings still require final adoption by EU foreign ministers.

Ukraine National Guard Uses Drones to Evacuate Oleshky Kittens in ‘Operation Tiger’ — Ukraine’s 11th National Guard Brigade used heavy drones to evacuate one cat and five kittens from besieged Oleshky across the Dnipro on Oct. 5-6. The rescue, dubbed “Operation Tiger,” came during a wider drone aid effort to deliver food and medicine.

Russia's September Jet Drones Use Spike to Nearly 3,500, Air Force Says — The spokesperson of Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched close to 3,500 jet-powered drones in September, up from the 2,850 documented in August. The numbers also mark a 10-fold spike from the 350 documented in June, with an estimated 1,600 launched in the last week of September alone. For now, Ukraine’s answers are F-16s and AI gun turrets.

Ukraine Warns of Russian Disinformation Over Oleshky Crisis — Ukrainian intelligence on Wednesday warned of an upcoming Russian disinformation campaign at occupied Oleshky, slated for October or early November, against Kyiv. The city, under Russian occupation, is facing a humanitarian crisis, with 2,000 residents lacking basic supplies and unable to leave.

Sweden Sends Patriot to Poland to Guard Ukraine Aid Hub — Sweden will deploy a Patriot air defense system and approximately 100 troops to Rzeszów, Poland, to protect a NATO logistics hub used to deliver military and civilian assistance to Ukraine. The deployment will begin in December and could continue through the first half of 2027.

Putin’s Focus is Now French Elections — Russia is shifting toward an economic war designed to exhaust Ukraine and weaken European support. With the war potentially extending into 2028 and Ukraine facing a $32 billion financing gap in 2027, Europe should secure long-term funding now.

Russian Attack Leaves Unexploded Ballistic Missile Among Homes in Kyiv, Hits Film Studio and Bird Center — An unexploded Russian ballistic missile was found among residential buildings in Kyiv, prompting a complex demining operation. The overnight attack also damaged the Dovzhenko Film Studio, destroyed an ATL Autoservice warehouse, and wiped out a bird rehabilitation center in the Kyiv region.

Russia’s Birthday ‘Gift’ to Putin: 70 Missiles Strike Ukraine, Hitting Homes and Killing Civilians — Russia launched 70 missiles and attack drones across Ukraine on Vladimir Putin’s birthday, targeting Kyiv and 12 regions. At least 14 people, including four children, were killed in a destroyed apartment building in Pryluky, while the nationwide death toll reached at least 20.

Triumph of Common Sense: Dissecting the Carlson-Rees-Mogg Interview — Tucker Carlson’s interview with Rees-Mogg exposes a fundamental disagreement over sovereignty, international commitments and the responsibility to resist aggression. From Ukraine to the world wars, Carlson repeatedly scrutinizes the cost of resistance while explaining away the conduct that made it necessary.
British Defence Intelligence Update Ukraine 6 October , 2026 — Latest from the British Defence Intelligence.

For Putin’s 74th Birthday, Ukraine Counts Nearly 1.55 Million Russian Military Losses — Ukraine’s General Staff estimates Russia’s total personnel losses at nearly 1.55 million since the full-scale invasion, including 1,690 over the past day. The tally also includes more than 551,000 UAVs, 50,800 artillery systems, and 12,396 tanks.

‘The Happiest Soul on the Wing’: Remembering a Fallen Ukrainian Pilot — Marat Mambetov was a flight commander in Ukraine’s 40th “Ghost of Kyiv” Tactical Aviation Brigade. The heroic MiG-29 pilot lost his life on Oct. 1 while flying a combat mission in defense of Ukraine.

5 Ballistic Missiles, 117 Drones: Ukraine Repels Massive Russian Overnight Attack — Ukraine said its forces intercepted or suppressed 161 Russian targets, including five ballistic missiles, 39 cruise missiles, and 117 drones. The attack struck 18 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at five sites.

UN Rights Council Extends Probe Into Russia’s Abuses Despite Moscow’s Opposition — The UN Human Rights Council voted 21-5 to extend its special rapporteur’s mandate on rights abuses in Russia for another year. The resolution cited worsening repression, including arrests and harassment of people opposing Russia’s war in Ukraine.

How NATO Plans to Win: ‘Theory of Victory’ Against Russia to be Unveiled in Poland — NATO’s top commander in Europe will unveil a strategy for defeating a potential Russian attack on the alliance’s eastern flank. The plan draws on Ukraine’s war experience, emphasizing low-cost drones, AI targeting and rapid strikes on Russian command systems.

Russian Aerial Assault Kills 25 in Ukraine, 4 Kids Among Dead as Pryluky Apartment Building Collapses — Russia launched a massive overnight missile and drone attack across Ukraine, killing 24 people. Strikes severely damaged a five-story apartment building in Pryluky, 150 km east of Kyiv, and caused extensive damage to homes and infrastructure in Kremenchuk.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 6, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 6, 2026.

Putin Reaches 74 as the CIS Hits 35 – or What Is Left of It — As Vladimir Putin marks his 74th birthday and the CIS approaches its 35th anniversary, the organization offers a stark measure of Russia’s declining influence across the former Soviet space. Several former members have left, while others are increasingly asserting political independence from Moscow.

Kim Jong Un Calls Russia’s War in Ukraine ‘Sacred’ in Putin Birthday Message — Kim Jong Un pledged continued support for Russia and called Moscow’s war against Ukraine a “sacred war of justice” in a birthday letter to Vladimir Putin. The message comes as thousands of North Korean troops have fought alongside Russian forces and Seoul estimates around 6,000 have been killed or wounded.

Kyiv Rocked by Repeated Russian Missile Attacks Overnight, 2 Killed After Zelensky’s ‘Massive Strike’ Warning — Kyiv was hit by repeated waves of Russian missile attacks overnight, with damage reported across several districts and a second round of explosions before dawn. The assault followed Zelensky’s warning that Moscow was preparing a “massive strike.”

Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker Burns off Sochi After Black Sea Attack — A Liberian-flagged oil tanker linked by Ukraine to Russia’s shadow fleet caught fire off Sochi after what Russian authorities described as an attack by an unmanned vessel. All 23 crew members were rescued as flames and thick black smoke spread across the coast.

Trump to Speak With Putin Over Siberia Plague Scare as US Pressure on Moscow Mounts — Trump says he will speak with Putin “very soon” as Washington and the WHO press Moscow for more information over the unexplained death of a worker at a Siberian anti-plague research institute.

Zelensky Awards Hero of Ukraine Title to Fallen ‘Ghost of Kyiv’ MiG-29 Pilot — President Zelensky has posthumously awarded the Hero of Ukraine title to 25-year-old MiG-29 pilot Marat Mambetov, who was killed in combat on Oct. 1 after his aircraft was struck by a Russian missile.

Zelensky Warns of Massive Russian Strike as 3 Tu-160 Bombers Take Off — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned on Tuesday evening that new intelligence points to Russian preparations for a massive strike, urging Ukrainians to heed air raid alerts. Hours later, Ukraine’s Air Force reported three Tu-160 strategic bombers taking off, saying possible cruise missiles could enter Ukrainian airspace after 3 a.m. local time.

Russia Behind Drone Strikes on Ships Off Bulgaria, Zelensky Says, as Radev Rules Out Invoking NATO Articles — Two civilian ships were hit by drones in Bulgaria’s Black Sea economic zone overnight, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. Citing contacts with Bulgaria’s navy, he pinned the blame for the strikes on Russia, while Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the drones’ origin was still unclear and ruled out invoking NATO’s Articles 4 and 5.

Ukraine Rejects Permanent EU Limits on Its Farm Exports After Accession — The European Commission proposed limiting Ukraine’s access to EU farm subsidies and markets for sensitive products even after accession, which Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi rejected on Tuesday, Oct. 5. by saying that Kyiv cannot accept permanent restrictions. Instead, he offered time-limited transition periods and pitched Ukraine as a supplier that could strengthen EU food security.

Lithuania Moves Closer Toward Scrapping Nuclear Weapons Ban — Lithuania moved closer toward lifting its long-standing nuclear weapons ban, after the amendment passed its first reading on Tuesday, Oct. 6, with 106-18 votes in favor. The country’s Constitution currently prohibits weapons of mass destruction and foreign military bases to be stationed on its territory. A final vote, scheduled for Jan. 12, 2027, could remove that provision. The Kremlin promptly responded to the move, calling any such

Russia Holds Major Nuclear Drill, Simulates Twin-Reactor Accident at Beloyarsk Plant — The Beloyarsk nuclear plant in Russia’s Sverdlovsk region began a two-day drill on Tuesday, Oct. 6, simulating a natural disaster and simultaneous accidents at two reactors. The exercise comes as the Kremlin escalates nuclear threats against Europe, including Lithuania, whose parliament voted the same day to lift its nuclear weapons ban.

Russia’s Jet Drones Could Reach 900 Km/h, Air Force Warns — Ukraine’s Air Force expects Russia could increase the speed of its jet-powered attack drones to 800-900 kilometers per hour, although such speeds have not yet been observed. Moscow is also expected to expand its use of jet drones, forcing Kyiv to accelerate interceptor production and rely heavily on F-16 fighters.

Ukrgasbank Appoints Former Deputy Finance Minister as New CEO — Artem Shevalev, a former deputy finance minister, has been appointed CEO of the state-owned Ukrgasbank, pending the central bank’s approval. His appointment ends over three years of interim leadership, with Volodymyr Ponomariov serving as acting CEO.

Rubio Calls on Russia to Clarify Suspected Plague Case — The US secretary of state urged Russia to provide more information about a suspected plague case in Siberia while warning against speculation. The call came after a lab worker died and nearly 200 people were reportedly placed under observation, although plague has not been confirmed.

South Korea Faces Questions Over Russia Fuel Shipments — South Korean ports reportedly handled over 176,000 tonnes of fuel bound for Russia in July and August, including shipments via sanctioned tankers. The news coincides with Seoul’s threats of further action against Kyiv over the latter’s disclosure of two North Korean POWs transferred to South Korea.

Freeze or Liberation? How Ukrainians Expect the War to End — A KIIS poll found that 41% of Ukrainians now consider preserving independence while leaving some territory occupied the most realistic end to the war, up from 33% in February 2025. Another 53% selected scenarios involving the liberation of at least some occupied land.

Fresh Intelligence Signals Massive Russian Strike Ahead, Zelensky Says — On Tuesday, Ukrainian intelligence received news that Russia is preparing a massive strike, prompting Kyiv to strengthen air defenses and other countermeasures. Zelensky said Ukraine is securing ammunition and interceptor missiles but remains entirely dependent on foreign partners for critical defenses against ballistic missiles.

2 Months Under Drapaty: Ukraine’s Army Is Winning — Drapaty is reshaping Ukraine’s military around drone-heavy warfare, decentralized command, and younger combat leaders. His tenure has seen local counteroffensives regain ground while pursuing a 30-year plan to modernize the AFU.

Ukraine’s Tech Sector Sets Sights on Growth at Kharkiv Forum Despite Russian Attacks — At the Global Tech Kharkiv forum, Credit Agricole is finalizing its Bank Lviv acquisition, Brave1 is redirecting Hr.7 billion ($159 million) to component production, Diia.City is adding BioTech and MedTech, and UK Aid is funding frontline SME software upgrades.

Ukraine Busts ‘Breaking Bad’ Labs Exporting Methadone Disguised as Car Fluid — Ukraine’s National Police dismantled two alleged drug networks during an operation named “Breaking Bad.” Investigators say one laboratory produced more than 10 kilograms (22 pounds) of methadone monthly and planned to export it disguised as automotive fluid, while mobile laboratories produced amphetamine for sale in Ukraine and Moldova.

Ukraine’s First Reconnaissance Drone ‘Furia’ Gets Its Own Postage Stamp — Ukraine’s Ukrposhta and drone maker Athlon Avia have released a new postage stamp series chronicling the history of the Furia, Ukraine’s first fixed-wing reconnaissance drone. The six-stamp sheet traces the UAV’s journey from its first combat deployments in 2014 to its use today by more than 100 Ukrainian brigades.

Russia Continues to Develop Cheap Cruise Missile Substitutes — The latest ISW report says Russia is increasing the use and development of inexpensive, jet-powered “quasi-cruise” missiles to step up its attacks on Ukraine. The speed and maneuverability offered by these weapons, in increasing numbers, are pressuring Ukraine’s air defenses.

Ukraine Claims Record Barrage on Russia With 1,750 Drones, 17 Flamingo Missiles — Ukraine launched a record-breaking barrage against Russia over 24 hours, with Moscow claiming its forces destroyed 1,750 Ukrainian drones and 17 Flamingo cruise missiles. The reported figures surpass the previous record for Ukrainian drone attacks and mark an unprecedented number of Flamingo missiles used in a single day.

Russian Supply Route Under Strain as Chonhar Bridge Span Collapses — Satellite images show major damage and a collapsed span on the Chonhar bridge linking occupied Crimea and the Kherson region, potentially complicating Russian military supply movements.

Lithuanian PM Warns Europe Against Ukraine War Fatigue — Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius urged NATO to develop a concrete plan for responding to Russian hybrid attacks, warning that Moscow is testing the alliance beyond its eastern flank. He said the threat includes drones, GPS interference, sabotage, and weaponized migration.

‘Situation Is Changing Dynamically’: Ukraine Says It Holds Tactical Initiative Near Vovchansk — Ukraine says it holds the tactical initiative near Vovchansk, while cautioning against confirming reported gains east of the city as fighting remains concentrated in a rapidly shifting gray zone, a Ukrainian military spokesperson said.

Power Cuts Return After Russian Strikes Damage Grid — Ukrenergo said scheduled hourly power cuts would return to parts of Ukraine from 3 p.m. until the end of Tuesday, Oct. 6, after Russian strikes damaged energy infrastructure. Restrictions will affect households and industry infrastructure, although the grid operator did not identify the regions covered.

Ship Sunk Off Bulgaria’s Economic Zone in Latest Black Sea Drone Attack — Two commercial ships were hit by drones off Bulgaria on Tuesday, with one sinking and its crew missing. The strikes followed attacks on commercial vessels near Turkey and Odesa as Kyiv and Moscow escalate their drone war in the Black Sea, with Russia retaliating for Ukrainian attacks on its refineries by targeting commercial vessels near Ukraine.

South Korea May Recall Ambassador Over Zelensky’s North Korean POW Disclosure — Seoul says Ukraine’s apology after revealing the transfer of two North Korean prisoners at the UN General Assembly fell short of expectations and is weighing diplomatic measures, including recalling its ambassador. Despite Seoul’s initial criticism, Kyiv said it had informed the former of its intention prior to the speech.

Poland to Deploy Patriot Battery Near Ukrainian Border — Poland will deploy one Patriot battery in the Lublin region near Ukraine as part of a broader military buildup. Warsaw is also expanding units, drone capabilities and aviation infrastructure across the region.

Russia Strikes Kryvyi Rih Hospital, 3 Wounded — Russian forces attacked central Kryvyi Rih with two Banderol loitering munitions on Tuesday, striking the grounds of a city hospital. Three people were wounded, including a hospital employee in serious condition and a woman who was walking her dog.

Russia Tests Balloon Barriers to Snare Ukrainian Drones — Russia has begun testing balloon barriers designed to counter Ukrainian drones, using Kevlar strands suspended from cables to entangle drone propellers. The system could force drones to fly higher, making them easier targets for Russian radar and air defenses.

As Ukraine Pushes, EU Weighs How to Absorb New Members — The European Commission is set to unveil proposals Tuesday aimed at addressing concerns over EU enlargement as Ukraine and three other candidates seek membership. The plans could include safeguards on voting rights and access to EU subsidies, amid fears enlargement could strain the bloc’s budget and decision-making.

Ukraine Targets Major Russian Oil Hub During Massive Drone Attack on Moscow Region — Ukraine launched a massive overnight drone attack on Moscow and the surrounding region, targeting what Russian investigative outlet Astra identified as a major oil depot supplying fuel to three Moscow airports. The strike came days after Ukraine hit another major Transneft oil hub.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 5, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 5, 2026.

Why Russia Wants Western Embassies Out of Kyiv – and Why They’re Staying — Russia has repeatedly warned foreign diplomats to leave Kyiv as attacks on the capital intensify. The US and European governments have rejected the pressure and kept their embassies open, denying Moscow the diplomatic isolation it appears to seek.

Trump Calls Russia’s Suspected Plague Case a ‘Big Problem’ as Nearly 200 Reportedly Monitored — Trump publicly addressed Russia’s suspected pneumonic plague case for the first time, calling it a “big problem.” CNN experts cited the scale of monitoring, FSB involvement and the lab’s history of military biological research as reasons for concern, while stressing that no weaponized pathogen has been confirmed.

Russian Strike Hits Zaporizhzhia Apartment Building, Injuring 5 — Russian forces struck an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, injuring two civilians. A 63-year-old man was hospitalized in serious condition, while a 37-year-old woman suffered thermal burns.

Russian Drones Sink Turkish-Owned Grain Ship as Ankara Pushes Black Sea Security Deal — Russian drones sank the Turkish-owned Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea, killing two crew members. The attack comes as Turkey and the UN push for a new maritime security arrangement. Ankara has also discussed Black Sea security with Azerbaijan.

Russian Drone Debris Falls Across Kyiv, Setting Cars Ablaze — Russian drone debris fell in two Kyiv districts Monday, destroying two cars and damaging another in Pecherskyi while debris also landed near homes in Solomianskyi.

Zelensky: Ukraine Securing New Air Defense Contracts, Scouring Globe for F-16 Ammo — Ukraine is preparing new contracts for air-defense systems and missiles while seeking additional anti-ballistic capabilities to protect critical infrastructure. Zelensky also said Kyiv is sourcing F-16 ammunition around the world, with new packages already on the way.
